class: a disclosed path-hygiene deviation by a subagent: private scratch written outside its own session scratchpad
severity: low. One disposable intermediate file, nothing under the worktree, nothing under SP, no listing and no glob, and the deliverable does not reference it - its builder re-derives every splice from the staged extract by exact path. Recorded because a disclosed deviation that goes unrecorded teaches the next execution that disclosure is optional.
disclosed_by: ezek_pr_LF_c05_a1#e1, in its own e19_selfreport, unprompted
what_happened: one earlier intermediate file of verified Hebrew splices was written to the Windows temp directory instead of a uniquely named subdirectory of the agent's own session scratchpad, which is where the launch message puts private scratch. The builder script itself went to the correct place.
what_did_NOT_happen: no listing, glob, wildcard or recursive search (E-19 clean, stated affirmatively)
no write under C:\wt\logos-t423-m8-fable and no write into SP
no receipt, no git command, no registry touch, no validator run
the deliverable does not read the misplaced file
why_it_matters_at_all: scratch location is not cosmetic: the session scratchpad is the space the campaign can account for and clean, and a stray file in a shared temp directory is outside every inventory the lifecycle policy keeps. At 44 executions the habit matters more than the file.
orchestrator_action: recorded, not remediated. The file is disposable, unreferenced and outside SP; hunting it would mean a listing of a shared temp directory, which is itself the thing E-19 forbids. The launch message already names the correct location, so no brief change is needed.
credit_where_due: the agent volunteered this in its own compliance self-report when nothing compelled it to. That is the behaviour the three-layer capture is for, and it is worth more than the defect costs.
limit: conduct record only; the packet's findings are unaffected and it landed with 0 form problems
